en.description:
Case Tracker for USCIS keeps your USCIS receipt numbers and the history of every status in one place, with civics test practice and shortcuts to the official USCIS and Department of State pages.

—— Your cases in one place ——

SAVE YOUR RECEIPTS
Save any USCIS receipt number and give it a name, so a family's petitions sit side by side.

STATUS HISTORY
The app does not fetch statuses from USCIS. Tap "Check on USCIS" to open the official USCIS Case Status page with your receipt number copied, then record the status it shows. Every status you record is kept on a timeline with its date and your notes, so you can see when your case actually moved. Copy a case summary to share it.

—— Know what is next ——

PROCESSING TIMES AND VISA BULLETIN
Shortcuts to the official USCIS processing-times page and the monthly Department of State visa bulletin.

NVC GUIDE
A stage-by-stage guide to the National Visa Center process after approval, with links to the State Department's CEAC site.

—— Prepare and understand ——

CIVICS TEST
Practise the official USCIS civics questions for both versions of the test: the 2025 test (128 questions, for N-400s filed on or after October 20, 2025) and the 2008 test (100 questions). A 65/20 filter shows only the 20 starred questions, and the trainer tracks what you have learned.

RESOURCES AND GOVERNMENT SOURCES
Plain-language answers to common questions, with a direct link to the official government page behind each one so you can verify it yourself.

NEWS FEED
The latest USCIS, ICE and CBP notices and rules published in the Federal Register.

—— Private ——

No sign-in. Your receipt numbers and status history are stored only on your device and are not sent to us.

—— Important ——

Case Tracker for USCIS is an independent app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by USCIS, the Department of State, or any government agency, and it does not provide legal advice. Always confirm anything that matters against the official government source, and consult a qualified immigration attorney about your own case.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
Case Tracker for USCIS keeps a person's USCIS receipt numbers and the history of each case's status on the device, with a civics test trainer and shortcuts to official USCIS and Department of State pages. The app does not fetch case statuses itself: the user checks the official USCIS Case Status website (opened from the app) and records the status in the app.

Intended audience:
People with a pending U.S. immigration case, and naturalization applicants preparing for the civics test.

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
There is no sign-in and no account in this version. After a three-page introduction (tap Skip or Next) the app opens on its tabs.
- My Cases tab: type any receipt number in the format ABC1234567890 (3 letters + 10 digits) and tap Add. Open the case, tap "Check on USCIS" to open the official site, and "Record status" to save a status to the case's history.
- Resources tab: Civics Test (choose the 2025 or 2008 test; the 65/20 filter shows the starred questions), NVC guide, News, and links to official processing times and the visa bulletin.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Google AdMob — advertising (with a consent prompt where required)
- Firebase Crashlytics and Analytics — crash reports and usage statistics
- Federal Register public API (federalregister.gov) — the news feed
- Links that open official government websites in the browser (uscis.gov, egov.uscis.gov, travel.state.gov, ceac.state.gov)
- Supabase (supabase.co) — bundled from the earlier version's sign-in and unused for new users: there is no sign-in screen in this version. It only restores the session of someone who signed in with an earlier version, so that person can delete the account (Settings > Delete Account). Google Sign-In and Sign in with Apple are bundled for the same reason and are not reachable.
Receipt numbers and status history are never sent off the device.

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app's interface is available in 9 languages: English, Spanish, Chinese (Simplified), Hindi, French, Arabic, Portuguese, Korean and Tagalog. Some screens are still partly in English. Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry. The civics questions and answers are the U.S. government's public-domain lists published by USCIS. All other content, artwork and copy are the developer's own. The app is not affiliated with any government agency and says so on its main screens.


ACCOUNT DELETION
The app has no sign-in and creates no account. Someone who created an account with an earlier version sees Settings > "Delete Account", which deletes that account. Data stays on the device: Profile > "Clear All Tracked Cases" removes the user's cases, and uninstalling removes everything.
